note: Open findings on shared baseline code and frozen contracts on main (bc957fd). Lane E cannot fix these (not owned; contracts are frozen). Every evidence key is produced by code and compared exactly in tests/test_baseline_findings.py, so a finding cannot appear or disappear without this file changing.

findings.title: Five of six frozen schemas have no $id, so they carry no machine-readable identity or version
findings.impact: Consumers cannot pin 'v0.1'; a future change is indistinguishable from the current schema.

findings.title: Timestamps are not required to be UTC and are only checked when a format checker is supplied
findings.impact: CONTRACTS.md demands UTC; '2026-01-05T11:00:00+02:00' validates. Without a format checker 'yesterday' validates too.
findings.proposed: RFC: add pattern 'Z$' (or document that consumers must run a strict checker); lane E enforces UTC-001 meanwhile.

findings.title: Required identifiers and free-text fields accept the empty string
findings.impact: ApplicationEvent.job_id = '' and ExperimentSpec.id = '' are schema-valid; referential checks then pass vacuously or collide.
findings.proposed: RFC: minLength 1 on required strings (JobPosting already does this for five fields); lane E enforces ID-001 meanwhile.

findings.title: ApplicationEvent, ExperimentSpec and AtlasPoint carry no subject or owner field
findings.impact: A payload cannot be attributed to a user, so cross-user export isolation cannot be verified from data; it must be enforced entirely by the storage layer. Acceptable for a single-user offline tool, blocking for any multi-user deployment.
findings.proposed: Owner decision before Phase 2: either stay single-user by design (documented) or RFC a subject_id on these three contracts.

findings.title: TransitionScenario.outputs is an untyped open object
findings.impact: Any key is legal, including offer_probability; the simulator's whole result is outside the contract. Lane E's PROB-001 lint is the only guard.
findings.proposed: RFC by C once the simulator output stabilises: type outputs (missing evidence, effort alternatives, uncertainty labels).

findings.title: Shared fixtures on main do not satisfy the frozen contracts they sit next to
findings.impact: All 4 records in fixtures/synthetic_jobs.json fail job-posting.schema.json (6 required fields missing, target_trajectory forbidden); there is no ProfileClaim fixture at all. A lane that develops against the fixtures builds to the wrong shape. Independently reported by A, C and D.
findings.proposed: Owner: replace the baseline fixtures with contract-valid ones (lane E's `python -m ctint.stub jobs.import` output is a candidate) or mark them legacy.

findings.title: score_job depends on a field the contract forbids and crashes on a field the contract makes optional
findings.impact: 45% of the reference score is target_trajectory (not in JobPosting; additionalProperties:false rejects it), and a contract-valid posting without remote_policy raises KeyError. The reference engine cannot rank contract-valid postings.
findings.proposed: Treat tools/reference_engine.py as a bootstrap demo only; lane A's matching replaces it. Do not let D or B call it.

findings.title: A NaN in an imported posting is scored as the maximum trajectory value
findings.impact: json.loads accepts NaN; min(1.0, NaN) is 1.0 in Python, so a poisoned feed can push any posting to the top of the reference ranking. The same number-handling trap applies to every lane that clamps untrusted floats.
findings.proposed: All lanes: reject non-finite numbers at import (parse_constant) and never clamp with min/max before checking isfinite.

findings.title: score_job and skill_gap disagree about skill case
findings.impact: A profile skill 'Python' is covered in the score but listed as a missing skill in the gap analysis.
findings.proposed: One normalisation function for skills, used by both (lane A owns the real implementation).

findings.title: assign_variant recomputation is unsafe under any design change and its key encoding is not injective
findings.impact: Reordering the variant list flips essentially every assignment; adding a third arm moves about a third of units between the two existing arms; (experiment_id, stratum) pairs containing U+241F collide; blank stratum / whitespace unit, salt, experiment id and variant are accepted. Safe only if assignments are journaled once and never recomputed.
findings.proposed: Lane B must journal assignments before exposure and hash a length-prefixed or JSON-encoded key (B's engine is reviewed separately). The reference function should not be used for real assignment.
